gaps.sentence: The protesters set ___ at dawn from the village square.
gaps.explanation: set off/out = begin a journey; set up = establish.

gaps.sentence: Many consumers now opt ___ cheaper brands.
Don't worry — he always turns ___ late.
gaps.explanation: turn up = arrive, often unexpectedly or late.

gaps.sentence: A new proposal was put ___ at the meeting.
gaps.explanation: put forward = propose, suggest (an idea, plan, name).

gaps.sentence: You should cut down ___ sugar if you want to lose weight.
gaps.explanation: cut down ON something = reduce it; cut out = eliminate completely.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to keep ___ with the latest slang.
gaps.explanation: keep up with = stay level with somebody/something changing.

gaps.sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: It's hard to reason ___ someone in a panic.
gaps.explanation: reason with somebody = try to persuade them logically.
